newsitem.title: FRANCE: McCann-Erickson ad agencies form Nordic venture.
newsitem.headline: McCann-Erickson ad agencies form Nordic venture.

text.p: Three Scandinavian advertising agencies owned by Interpublic's McCann-Erickson on Tuesday said they had formed a joint venture to focus on the pan-European advertising market.

The principals of the new network agency, at a news conference at the International Advertising Festival being held here this week, said the agency will focus on "high-impact creative solutions for companies doing business in Nordic and European countries."

Bo Ronnberg, president of Sweden's Ronnberg McCann, one of the three partners of the new network agency, said the concept is to create an "advertising lighthouse" for European companies. The other two partners of the new agency include Norway's JBR/McCann and Finland's hasan & partner.
The new agency, AD'AM-JBR/Ronnberg/hasan, will be based in Amsterdam.

"There are three big places (for advertising) in Europe -- France, Germany and Britain," Ronnberg told the news conference. "The French wouldn't understand why you would open in London. The British wouldn't understand why you would open in Paris, and so forth and so on. Amsterdam is a neutral place."
AD'AM will initially focus on attracting Nordic companies that are expanding globally and on global advertisers that are entering Nordic markets.

Petter Gudmundseth, chairman of JBR/McCann, told Reuters the new agency expects to be able to win pan-European accounts from Scandinavian companies that the three partners have not been able to win on their own.

"Why don't the big Scandinavian companies use us to do their European campaigns?" Gudmundseth asked. "They think we're too local. Hopefully, we will become more attractive to Nordic clients who today go to agencies in London."
Nordic companies surveyed in a research study done by McCann several months ago showed a very positive response to the concept of a Scandinavian agency.

Gudmundseth said he could not estimate the value of advertising accounts the new agency hopes to win, but noted, "If a Scandinavian client goes to BBH (Bartle, Bogle, Hegarty) in London they're probably paying two to three times...what they would pay us."
The new agency said its combined creative strength -- built on a Scandinavian tradition of making strong advertising statements -- will help build success.
"It's all about the great idea," said Gudmundseth. "A great idea will travel across borders."
The three partners have all made very small equity investments in AD'AM which will be a strictly creative agency but will have access to McCann's media planning, placement and global resources.
